There are two sources of vitamin D: the diet (where it is found as vitamin D2 (ergocalciferol) or vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol)) or
synthesis in skin during exposure to ultraviolet radiation (sunlight). The vitamin enters the circulation and is transported on
a vitamin D binding protein to the liver, where it is hydroxylated to 25(OH) vitamin Ddthe major circulating form of the vitamin.
It is hydroxylated again in the kidney to 1,25(OH)2 vitamin D, or calcitriol, the most active metabolite of the vitamin. Vitamin D
